answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.SOUP: Soup is served with its liquid. A broth can be part of a soup or served by itself.
answerNotes.RICE: Rice is a grain that absorbs water as it cooks. The word names the grain, not the pot or the cooking method.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.SHARE: Share means give part of something to others. In a meal setting it can concern food rather than dividing property or money.

answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.SONG: A song has words and a melody. In the familiar-title puzzles, ordinary definitions help even when a reader does not remember the recording.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.USHER: An usher helps people find seats. The role differs from the performers on stage or the clerk selling tickets.
answerNotes.PRINT: A print can be an image or an impression. In snow, it is the mark left by a foot or shoe rather than words on paper.

answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.AISLE: An aisle is a passage between rows. In a theater it lets people reach seats without climbing over them.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.HALL: Hall can mean an entrance passage or a large gathering room. A town hall is a public building, while a hallway is a passage.
answerNotes.SPEAKER: A speaker can be a person talking or an audio device. In a video call's controls, it is the device that makes sound audible.
answerNotes.CIRCLE: A circle is a round line or shape. In a marble game, a drawn circle can mark the playing area.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.

answerNotes.COFFEE: Coffee is brewed from roasted beans. The familiar beans are actually seeds from the coffee plant's fruit.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
answerNotes.CREAM: Cream is the rich part of milk. Whipping adds air, which is why whipped cream becomes fluffy.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.TAP: Tap can mean a faucet or a light knock. The water-container scene uses the faucet meaning.
answerNotes.HALL: Hall can mean an entrance passage or a large gathering room. A town hall is a public building, while a hallway is a passage.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
